=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:741 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The detached reporter reads the last log record of the file rather than receiving the specific record that triggered it.
  WHY: The detached reporter starts with a non-blocking Popen and returns immediately. If two PermissionRequest events fire in rapid succession, the second record can be appended to the session log before the first reporter starts its Python interpreter. Both reporters will read record B, and record A will be silently lost from the immediate reporting path.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:760-770 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The GitHub POST operation is performed before the local deduplication state is saved.
  WHY: If local state-file saving (immediate-state.json or filed-state.json) fails after a successful network POST (e.g., due to a read-only mount, disk-full, or filesystem permissions error), the local reservation is not recorded. Subsequent file_patterns calls or report_now attempts will not see the signature as reported and will produce duplicate GitHub issues or comments.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:503-514 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The filing_lock uses fcntl.flock on independently opened file descriptors.
  WHY: On Linux, flock locks are associated with the open file description, not the inode. When separate reporter and file processes open filing.lock independently via Path.open("a"), they each receive different file descriptions. As a result, both processes can acquire their own independent exclusive lock on the file simultaneously. This allows concurrent read-modify-write operations on state files, leading to lost report records or state corruption.
- .claude/hooks/permission_prompt_logger.py:98-109 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The hook spawns a detached subprocess on every PermissionRequest without an explicit kill switch or feature flag.
  WHY: If the detached reporter process encounters issues (e.g., API failures, hangs, resource leaks), there is no runtime way to disable this path short of reverting the hook file, which is a production safety risk.
